purpose: Practical tutorials for experiments with synthetic land records, validation workflows, geospatial checks, document extraction, model evaluation, and dataset publication.

data_policy.privacy: Never include real Aadhaar numbers, private land records, personal identifiers, credentials, or other sensitive personal data.
data_policy.authority_boundary: This is an experimental decision-support project, not an official land registry or a substitute for verification by the competent revenue authority.
data_policy.legal_traceability: Mark rules as verified only when linked to a current authoritative source and reviewed for jurisdiction and effective date. Label synthetic assumptions explicitly.

tutorials.title: Generate a Reproducible Synthetic Land-Record Dataset
tutorials.objective: Generate fictional parcel, survey, document, and transaction records that can be recreated with a fixed random seed.
steps: Define field names, types, required fields, and allowed values before generating records.
Use fictional names and synthetic identifiers; never derive identifiers from real people or official records.
Set and record a random seed so the same configuration can reproduce the dataset.
Generate normal cases and controlled edge cases, including missing fields, duplicate references, and conflicting area values.
Export JSONL or CSV and write a manifest with row counts, schema version, seed, and generation timestamp.
experiment_ideas: Compare datasets with 100, 1000, and 10000 records.
Vary the rate of missing and conflicting fields.
Regenerate the same dataset twice and compare hashes.
validation_checks: Every record conforms to the declared schema.
The seed and generator configuration are recorded.
All generated records are labelled synthetic.
safety_notes: Do not use real Aadhaar numbers or real personal data.
Do not imply fictional parcel identifiers refer to official records.

tutorials.title: Design Relational Schemas and Check Referential Integrity
tutorials.objective: Model parcels, parties, document references, survey records, and transaction events without confusing person identity with parcel identity.
steps: Define separate entities for parcels, parties, documents, survey observations, and transaction events.
Assign stable synthetic IDs and define relationships between entities.
Declare unique, required, optional, and repeatable fields.
Check orphaned references, duplicate primary IDs, and invalid relationship cardinality.
Document the difference between parcel boundaries, ownership claims, and historical transactions.
experiment_ideas: Inject orphaned document references and measure detection.
Compare normalized relational records with nested JSON.
Test joint ownership and multiple historical transactions.
validation_checks: All references resolve or are explicitly marked unresolved.
Primary IDs are unique.
A person identifier is never used as the parcel primary key.
safety_notes: Use fictional parties and identifiers.
Schema validity does not prove legal ownership.

tutorials.title: Normalize Land-Record Fields and Units
tutorials.objective: Standardize text, dates, units, and field formats while retaining original values for auditability.
steps: Preserve each source value in a raw or source-value field.
Create normalized fields for whitespace, casing, date formats, and known spelling variants.
Define explicit area-unit conversions and store both original and converted units.
Flag ambiguous dates, unsupported units, and values outside configured bounds.
Record each transformation and its rule version in a log.
experiment_ideas: Measure normalization accuracy on noisy synthetic fields.
Test equivalent areas expressed in different supported units.
Compare strict rejection with review-required handling for ambiguous values.
validation_checks: Raw values remain available.
Unit conversions are tested against known examples.
Ambiguous values are flagged rather than silently guessed.
safety_notes: Do not silently overwrite source evidence.
Verify jurisdiction-specific units and conventions before real-world use.

tutorials.title: Match Parcel References Across Synthetic Documents
tutorials.objective: Compare parcel references across sources and explain why records match or conflict.
steps: Choose candidate fields such as synthetic parcel ID, survey reference, village code, and document date.
Define exact-match rules before introducing fuzzy matching.
Generate pairs with known labels: match, partial match, mismatch, missing, and review required.
Run matching rules and store field-level comparisons and rule identifiers.
Return an explanation and evidence references for each result.
experiment_ideas: Compare exact matching with weighted scoring.
Vary typo and missing-field rates.
Measure false matches when only a weak field agrees.
validation_checks: Every result has a status and explanation.
Conflicts are not hidden by an overall score.
Ambiguous cases can be routed to human review.
safety_notes: A technical match is not a legal ownership determination.
Do not merge records solely because names are similar.

tutorials.title: Create Ground-Truth Labels for Validation Experiments
tutorials.objective: Build a labelled test set that measures validation performance and distinguishes automated findings from human review.
steps: Write a labelling guide defining MATCH, PARTIAL_MATCH, MISMATCH, MISSING, and REVIEW_REQUIRED.
Create balanced examples, including edge cases and insufficient-evidence cases.
Keep expected labels separate from model inputs to prevent label leakage.
Have an independent reviewer or rule set audit a sample of labels.
Version the label guide and record the rationale for each label.
experiment_ideas: Compare performance by status class.
Measure reviewer agreement on ambiguous examples.
Test whether a model over-predicts MATCH when one field agrees.
validation_checks: Each example has a documented expected label.
Label fields are excluded from inference inputs.
Ambiguous cases are represented rather than discarded.
safety_notes: Labels describe synthetic experiments, not official legal determinations.

tutorials.title: Validate Synthetic Parcel Geometry with GeoJSON
tutorials.objective: Check synthetic parcel polygons for geometry validity, coordinate ranges, and area consistency.
prerequisites: A geospatial library such as Shapely or GeoPandas
steps: Generate clearly fictional polygons that do not expose a real private parcel.
Declare the coordinate reference system; GeoJSON commonly uses WGS 84 longitude and latitude.
Check coordinate ranges, ring closure, polygon validity, and empty geometries.
Calculate area in a suitable projected coordinate system or with an appropriate geodesic method; do not treat square degrees as square metres.
Compare calculated area with the synthetic declared area using a documented tolerance.
experiment_ideas: Inject self-intersections, open rings, and out-of-range coordinates.
Compare declared and computed areas under different tolerances.
Test transformations between geographic and projected coordinate systems.
validation_checks: CRS assumptions are recorded.
Invalid geometries are flagged.
Area calculations document method and unit.
safety_notes: These checks do not certify legal boundaries or replace survey and authority verification.

tutorials.title: Benchmark OCR and Document-Field Extraction
tutorials.objective: Evaluate extraction of selected fields from synthetic scans against annotated ground truth.
prerequisites: Synthetic sample documents or generated document images
steps: Create synthetic document images with fictional values, varied layouts, and varied scan quality.
Annotate expected field values and bounding boxes where applicable.
Run OCR or extraction and store raw text separately from parsed fields.
Normalize extracted values using documented rules and compare them field by field with ground truth.
Report exact-match accuracy, character error rate where relevant, and omission, substitution, and field-confusion errors.
experiment_ideas: Vary blur, rotation, contrast, and resolution.
Compare layouts and fonts where licensing permits.
Measure field-level accuracy for dates, area values, and reference numbers.
validation_checks: Raw OCR output is preserved.
Metrics use held-out annotations.
Extraction uncertainty is surfaced.
safety_notes: Do not upload confidential real documents to unapproved services.
OCR output is a candidate extraction, not verified evidence.

tutorials.title: Represent Transaction Chronology and Conflicting Events
tutorials.objective: Represent synthetic transaction events as a timeline and detect date-ordering or reference inconsistencies.
steps: Represent each event with a synthetic event ID, parcel reference, event type, date, source reference, and provenance.
Keep event occurrence dates separate from ingestion and processing timestamps.
Define checks for missing dates, configured impossible sequences, and duplicate event references.
Generate conflicting and incomplete timelines for testing.
Explain the triggered rule and route unresolved legal or factual conflicts to review.
experiment_ideas: Inject out-of-order dates and duplicate events.
Test date-format handling.
Compare strict chronology rules with review-required handling for uncertain event types.
validation_checks: Source and processing timestamps are distinct.
Events are not silently deleted to make timelines consistent.
Each issue includes a rule reference.
safety_notes: Chronology checks alone do not establish title, priority, or legal effect.

tutorials.title: Build a Traceable Validation-Rule Catalogue
tutorials.objective: Make validation rules versioned, testable, explainable, and traceable to verified sources or explicitly labelled synthetic assumptions.
steps: Give every rule a stable ID, title, description, severity, applicable fields, and version.
Record jurisdiction, source title, official URL, publication or effective date, and review status for legal or administrative sources.
Clearly mark unverified, illustrative, or synthetic rules; do not present them as law.
Create positive, negative, and boundary tests for every rule.
Include rule IDs and explanations in results alongside the evidence fields used.
experiment_ideas: Compare results before and after a rule-version change.
Check whether each result traces to a rule version.
Test behaviour when a source is missing or out of date.
validation_checks: Every rule has a stable ID and version.
Legal claims have a traceable authoritative source and review status.
Synthetic assumptions are distinguished from verified requirements.
safety_notes: Do not invent citations, statutes, or official integrations.
This catalogue is not legal advice.

tutorials.title: Split Data Without Leakage
tutorials.objective: Create training, validation, and test partitions that avoid related records leaking across splits.
prerequisites: A stable group or source identifier
steps: Identify grouping keys such as parcel family, document template, or generated case lineage.
Split by group when related records could otherwise appear in multiple partitions.
Stratify by status where practical without breaking group boundaries.
Fit normalization, vocabulary, and other learned preprocessing on training data only.
Record split seed, proportions, group keys, and class distributions in a manifest.
experiment_ideas: Compare random-row splits with group-aware splits.
Measure performance after removing near-duplicates from test data.
Repeat experiments with multiple seeds.
validation_checks: No group appears in multiple partitions.
Preprocessing is fitted on training data only.
The split is reproducible from its manifest.
safety_notes: Strong synthetic-data scores do not guarantee performance on real-world records.

tutorials.title: Evaluate Validation Models and Rules
tutorials.objective: Measure classification quality and error patterns instead of relying on overall accuracy alone.
steps: Calculate a confusion matrix for all supported validation statuses.
Report per-class precision, recall, and F1, plus macro and weighted averages where appropriate.
Inspect false MATCH outcomes separately.
For scored predictions, evaluate calibration and choose review thresholds using validation data only.
Publish limitations, test-set composition, and failure examples with the metrics.
experiment_ideas: Compare rule-based, heuristic, and machine-learning baselines.
Tune review thresholds and report review workload.
Evaluate performance as missing fields and OCR errors increase.
validation_checks: Metrics use held-out data.
Per-class results are reported.
Thresholds are not tuned on the final test set.
safety_notes: Model confidence is not legal confidence.
Keep human review for ambiguous or high-impact conflicts.

tutorials.title: Audit Dataset Quality, Privacy, and Reproducibility
tutorials.objective: Produce a quality report and provenance manifest before sharing a dataset.
steps: Check required fields, types, allowed values, duplicate IDs, and cross-record references.
Scan for accidental personal data, real identifiers, secrets, local paths, and unintended metadata.
Calculate file checksums and record schema and generator versions.
Report class balance, missingness, duplicate rates, and known limitations.
Keep a machine-readable manifest alongside a human-readable dataset card.
experiment_ideas: Inject known defects and verify the audit catches them.
Compare schema versions and generate a migration report.
Check reproducibility using the same seed.
validation_checks: Published files are enumerated in the manifest.
Quality checks have pass/fail outcomes.
Synthetic status and limitations are documented.
safety_notes: Do not publish private records or credentials.
Audit synthetic data for accidentally copied real information.

tutorials.title: Prepare a Kaggle-Ready Dataset Package
tutorials.objective: Package synthetic experiments with clear documentation, reproducible files, and responsible-use notes.
steps: Choose file names and formats such as CSV, JSONL, or GeoJSON according to the data structure.
Include a README or dataset card covering purpose, generation method, fields, limitations, and intended use.
Include a schema, validation report, licence decision, and reproducibility details.
Check that examples are synthetic and do not imply unsupported official endorsement.
Review Kaggle's current upload, licensing, privacy, and content requirements before publishing.
experiment_ideas: Compare CSV and JSONL usability.
Ask another person to reproduce an experiment from the published instructions.
Run a clean-environment smoke test.
validation_checks: Files match the manifest.
Licence and source statements are accurate.
Synthetic status and limitations are clearly disclosed.
safety_notes: Do not imply government provenance or legal authority unless demonstrably true.
Verify current platform requirements before uploading.

tutorials.title: Integrate Synthetic Fixtures into the LANDSYNC AI Application
tutorials.objective: Use a small versioned synthetic fixture set to test API and UI validation flows.
steps: Create a fixture pack with at least one example for each validation status.
Validate fixtures against the backend schema before importing them.
Use a development-only loader or test fixture mechanism, not production data.
Test response fields, evidence references, rule IDs, explanations, and review flags.
Add regression tests to preserve expected behaviour as the application changes.
experiment_ideas: Test missing and malformed request fields.
Check that the UI distinguishes automated findings from review-required cases.
Test API compatibility after a schema change.
validation_checks: Fixtures are synthetic and development-only.
API responses match the documented contract.
Expected results are asserted in automated tests.
safety_notes: Do not connect experimental fixtures to an official registry or mutate authoritative records.
Keep real integrations disabled unless separately authorized and verified.
